chunks: Ja'far b. Ali b. al-Hasan b. Ali b. Abdullah b. al-Mughira al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan b. Ali narrated to us from his grandfather Abdullah b. al-Mughira from Isma'il b. Muslim from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said:

When the scholars and wise men of the past wrote to one another, they wrote only about three things, without a fourth: Whoever is worried about the Hereafter, God will take care of his worries in this world. Whoever rectifies his inner self, God will rectify his outer self. Whoever rectifies that which is between him and God, Mighty and Majestic, God will rectify for him that which is between him and the people.

key_terms.الآخرة: The Hereafter — the afterlife, the eternal abode
key_terms.سريرة: Inner self — one's hidden spiritual state, intentions, and conscience
key_terms.علانية: Outward/public self — one's visible conduct and reputation among people

ai.seo_question: What three principles did the early scholars write about according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali reports a tradition of the early scholars and wise men who, when corresponding with one another, would only write about three things with no fourth: whoever makes the Hereafter his primary concern, God will take care of his worldly concerns; whoever rectifies his inner self, God will rectify his outward appearance; and whoever rectifies his relationship with God, God will rectify his relationship with people. This was presented as the distilled wisdom of generations of scholars, conveying three interconnected principles of spiritual development.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ja`far b. `Ali b. al-Hasan b. `Ali b. `Abdullah b. al-Mughira al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan b. `Ali narrated to us from his grandfather `Abdullah b. al-Mughira from Isma`il b. Muslim from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: Amir al-Mu’minin (as) said:

When the scholars and the wisemen of the past wrote to one another, they wrote only about three things, without a fourth: (1) Whoever is worried about the Hereafter, Allah will take care of his worries in this world. (2) Whoever rectifies his inner self, Allah will rectify his outer self. (3) Whoever rectifies that which is between him and Allah, Allah will rectify that which is between him and the people.
